title: Sailing beneath a sea of stars
caption: The Extremely Large Telescope under construction beneath the stars, Cerro Armazones, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at the ELT site, Cerro Armazones, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Under a star-filled sky, ESO's Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) sits on top of Cerro Armazones in Chile, like a ship riding the crest of a huge, shadowy wave. Its dome is illuminated, and a thin white line above it is one of the cranes around the construction site.

It's an unusual angle on the telescope. The photographer stood at the Rolf Chini Cerro Murphy Observatory, a neighbouring facility that ESO's Paranal Observatory hosts. The familiar cranes around the building work are also visible.

The ELT is due to be finished at the end of the decade. Then it will start probing this sea of stars, which ESO counts among the most pristine skies on the planet, above a desert with a rich and important heritage of skywatching.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based landscape photograph credited to P. Romaniuk/ESO. The source does not publish camera, exposure or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the star field may look richer here than it would to an observer at Cerro Murphy.
